# $P_n=\star2$ for every even $n\ge 8$ (whole-board game)

**Summary**
1. Theorem: in the whole-board game on $C_n$ (race rule "count", e.p. on, an e.p.-capturable pawn is not passed, the game ends at the first passed pawn) $P_n=\star2$ for every even $n\ge8$; $P_n$ has $n+2$ pawns. "$=\star2$" has the meaning of Section S13: $P_n+\star h$ and $\star2+\star h$ have the same outcome for every nim-heap (H8).
2. The proof is that of Section S13: Lemmas 1-3 are quoted in section 2 with one repaired definition ("pattern file"), and the proof of Lemma 3 (ii)-(iii), which Section S13 gives in two terse lines, is written out in section 2b. The wall of $P_n$ is E-type ($W2/B4$) on files $6..n-1$; cut $c=12$, base case $n_0=18$.
3. Every hypothesis of Lemmas 2 and 3 holds for $P_n$ (section 3). The argument of Section S13 uses only the wall, the zone and the cut; the wall phase, its two ends and the zone location differ from $E_n$, and none of them enters (one end case, the double step of $W2$ on file $n-2$ at $n=18$, is L instead of P; H2).
4. Finite checks, by 3-5 programs each (section 4): C1' the reduced game $R_{18}$ has 813 nodes, no e.p. flag, zone $\{0,2,3,4,5,6\}$, and $G+\star2$ is a P-position; C2' $P_n+\star2$ is a P-position for $n=8,10,12,14,16$. Two further programs (section 7) rebuilt everything and found no difference, for all even $n\le60$.
5. Status: PROVED for even $n\ge18$ given Lemmas 1-3 of Section S13, the new text of 2b, and C1'; CHECKED-2 for $n=8..16$.

**How this note was checked.** The finite parts were computed by five independently written programs, A to E (section 0): A is the C program of Section S13; B rebuilds the reduced graphs on the project's game library `cylcgt`; C, D and E are Python engines written from the rules, C for the check of Section S13, D and E for the check of this note. All five recomputed C1'; A, C, D and E recomputed C2'; C, D and E also tested Lemmas 2 and 3 on the actual nodes or on random positions. The hand proof was checked by two adversarial AI reviewers of the same model family as the model that wrote the note, one for the logic and one for the computations, which found no mathematical defect; the corrections they asked for (a missing heap step, the definition of pattern file, the written-out step (iii), an end case, labels and caveats) are incorporated in the text. Section 2b, the only new mathematics, was then refereed by one AI referee from a different model vendor, which found it sound. No human referee has checked the note yet.

**Scope.** Proved: the whole-board game, race rule "count" (not "mover"), and equivalence to $\star2$ against nim-heaps (H8). Not claimed: the component-sum model of `cylcgt` (192 of the 813 nodes of $R_{18}$ split into components), another race rule, odd $n$ (this note is about even $n$ only), or equivalence against arbitrary addends.

## 0. Claims and labels
PROVED = by hand, given the lemmas. CHECKED-2 = two or more independently written programs agree (the programs are listed in each row). COMPUTED-1 = one program.
Programs: **A** = the program `rg.c` of Section S13 (C, unchanged); **B** = `reduced_cyl.py`, a rebuild on `cylcgt`'s `pawns.moves/passed/_child`; **C** = `check3/eng.py`, the Python engine written for the check of Section S13 (written from the rules, independent of A and B); **D** = `verify_logic/engine.py`, a fresh engine written from the rules for the logic check of this note; **E** = `verify_compute/myeng.py`, a fresh engine written from the `pawns.py` rules for the computational check of this note (it shares only the position encoding with C, and was differentially tested against `pawns.moves/passed/promote_distance`: about 61k positions, 0 mismatches). All five were written from the same rule description, not from each other's code; a shared misreading of the rules is excluded only by that differential test.

## 1. Setting
Model, T/L/P/K classes and reduced game: exactly as in Section S13 (paragraph "Model"). Terminal = at least one side has a passed pawn; non-terminal = neither has. Race rule "count" (as implemented in `rg.c` and in `cylcgt/pawns.py`, `RACE_RULE = "count"`): if both have one after a move of $X$, the side with the smaller promotion distance wins, ties to $Y$ (who did not just move). The distance is the minimum over the side's passed pawns that are the front pawn of their file and not e.p.-capturable; $d=8-r-[r=2]$ (white, rank $r$), $d=r-1-[r=7]$ (black).
$P_n$ ($n$ even $\ge8$), files $0..n-1$: $W5,\ B7,\ W4,\ W4B7,\ B6,\ W3B6$, then $(W2,B4)^{(n-6)/2}$. File $j\ge6$ holds $W2$ if $j$ is even, $B4$ if $j$ is odd. $R_n$ = reduced game of $G_n=P_n$ (nodes = positions with flag reachable by K-moves), $\mathrm{start}_n$ its root. $\mathrm{ins}_c$ as in Lemma 3.

## 2. The lemmas of Section S13 (statements quoted from Lemmas 1-3 there)
The statements of Lemmas 1-3 below are quoted verbatim. The definition they rely on was sharpened: Section S13 first said "a pattern file is a wall file that still holds its starting pawn", which does not exclude extra pawns on the file (it now says that a pattern file contains precisely its one starting wall pawn), and Lemma 2's proof ("neighbours of $q$ are pawns of the other colour two ranks further on") needs the exact content. Throughout this note:

**Pattern file.** A wall file whose content is *exactly* its starting pawn and nothing else. The wall is files $3..n-1$ of $O_n$, $E_n$, resp. files $6..n-1$ of $P_n$: single pawns alternating $W3/B5$ (O) or $W2/B4$ (E), black two ranks above white. A *wall pawn* is the pawn of a pattern file.

This is the reading the programs of Section S13 use (they compare file contents with equality).

**Lemma 1 (Reduction).** A side wins $G+\star h$ moving first iff it wins the reduced game moving first.
**Lemma 2 (Wall pawns).** Let $c$ have no passed pawn, with an e.p. flag (if any) protecting a pawn of the player not to move, and let $q$ be a wall pawn of the player $Z$ to move, with pattern files $j-1,j,j+1$. (a) After any move of $q$, $Z$ has no passed pawn. (b) If $c$ has no flag, $Z=X$, and files $j-1,\dots,j+3$ (or $j-3,\dots,j+1$) are pattern files, every move of $q$ is L or P.
**Lemma 3 (Insertion).** Let $p$ on $C_n$ have no passed pawn and no e.p. flag, and let files $c-4,\dots,c+5$ be pattern files. Let $\hat p=\mathrm{ins}_c(p)$ on $C_{n+2}$ be $p$ with two files, with the contents of files $c+1$ and $c$, inserted after file $c$ (the pattern continues). For each side, the children of its K-moves in $\hat p$ are the $\mathrm{ins}_c$-images of those in $p$, and it has a T-move in $\hat p$ iff in $p$.

### 2b. Proof of Lemma 3, written out (new text)
Section S13 proves Lemma 3 in six lines; its step (iii) cites (ii) for the replies of $Y$, although (ii) is about moves of $X$. What (iii) needs is the following, which is proved here from Lemma 2 and the view lemma V.

*Notation.* $\mathrm{ins}_c(q)$ has files $q_0..q_c$, then $q_{c+1}$ and $q_c$ (the two *new* files $c+1,c+2$), then the old files $q_{c+1},q_{c+2},\dots$ at places $c+3,c+4,\dots$ (old file $f\ge c+1$ moves to $f+2$). The pawns on old files are the *image* pawns. The *view* of a pawn is the contents of its own file and the two neighbouring files (the e.p. flag aside); a pawn's moves and its passed status depend on its view and the flag only. $\mathrm{ins}_c$ carries a flag along with its pawn.

**V (view lemma).** Let $q$ be any position on $C_n$. (V1) Every image pawn of $\mathrm{ins}_c(q)$ has the same view as its preimage in $q$ (the file left of old file $c+1$ is a copy of $q_c$, the file right of old file $c$ is a copy of $q_{c+1}$; nothing else changes). (V2) A new pawn has the view $(q_c,q_{c+1},q_c)$ or $(q_{c+1},q_c,q_{c+1})$. If files $c,c+1$ of $q$ are pattern files, these are views in which the pawn is blocked by both neighbours (pattern pawns of the other colour, two ranks further on), so new pawns are not passed. (V3) Hence, if files $c,c+1$ of $q$ are pattern files, the passed pawns of $\mathrm{ins}_c(q)$ are exactly the images of those of $q$, with the same colour, rank, own-file contents and e.p. protection. So $q$ and $\mathrm{ins}_c(q)$ are both non-terminal, or both terminal with the same winner (the race rule compares the same pawns, and the same side moved last). In particular $\hat p$ has no passed pawn.

*Proof of Lemma 3.* Let $X$ be the side to move and $Y$ the other. Put $A=\{c-4,\dots,c+5\}$, a set of pattern files of $p$; then $\{c-4,\dots,c+7\}$ are pattern files of $\hat p$.
(i) *Central pawns.* A pawn of $X$ on a file $j\in\{c-3,\dots,c+4\}$ of $p$ has its three files in $A$ and a five-file window $j-1..j+3$ (for $j\le c+2$) or $j-3..j+1$ (for $j\ge c-1$) inside $A$. By Lemma 2(b) ($p$ has no passed pawn and no flag) every move of it is L or P, so it is neither T nor K. The same holds in $\hat p$ for the pawns on files $c-3,\dots,c+6$ (the new pawns included), whose windows lie inside the pattern arc $c-4..c+7$ of $\hat p$.
(ii) *Far moves of $X$.* Every other pawn of $X$ in $p$ stands on a file $\le c-4$ or $\ge c+5$; it corresponds to a pawn of $\hat p$ on a file $\le c-4$ or $\ge c+7$, with the same moves (V1). A move $\mu$ of it touches only files $\le c-3$ or $\ge c+4$ (a capture changes the neighbouring file; the file of an e.p. victim is the destination file; a double step puts the flag on its own file). So files $c-2,\dots,c+3$ of the child $c_\mu$ are unchanged, files $c,c+1$ are pattern files, and $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$ is the child of the corresponding move $\hat\mu$. By V3, $c_\mu$ and $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$ are both non-terminal or both terminal with the same winner, i.e. $\mu$ and $\hat\mu$ are both T, both L, or both non-terminal.
(iii) *Poison.* Let $c_\mu$ be non-terminal. $\mu$ is P iff $Y$ has a reply $\nu$ with $c_\mu\nu$ terminal and won by $Y$ (then $Y$ has a passed pawn). Files $c-2,\dots,c+3$ of $c_\mu$ hold the pattern, and files $c-2,\dots,c+5$ of $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$ do. Call a pawn of $Y$ *near* if it stands on a file in $c-1..c+2$ of $c_\mu$ (resp. in $c-1..c+4$ of $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$, which contain the two new files), *far* otherwise (files $\le c-2$ or $\ge c+3$, resp. $\le c-2$ or $\ge c+5$).
- *Near replies.* A near pawn is a wall pawn whose files $j-1,j,j+1$ lie inside the pattern files just listed, and $c_\mu$ has no passed pawn and an e.p. flag (if any) protecting a pawn of $X$, the player not to move. By Lemma 2(a), after any near reply $Y$ has no passed pawn, so the result is not terminal-won by $Y$. This holds in $c_\mu$ and in $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$ alike.
- *Far replies.* The far pawns of $c_\mu$ and of $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$ correspond (V1), with the same moves. A far reply $\nu$ touches only files $\le c-1$ or $\ge c+2$ (a pawn on $c+3$ may capture onto $c+2$; one on $c-2$ onto $c-1$), so files $c,c+1$ of $c_\mu\nu$ are still pattern files and $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu\nu)$ is the child of $\hat\nu$. By V3, $c_\mu\nu$ is terminal-won by $Y$ iff $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu\nu)$ is. (The e.p. victim of an earlier far move $\mu$ sits on a file $\le c-4$ or $\ge c+5$, so e.p. replies are far replies.)

Hence $Y$ has a winning terminal reply to $\mu$ iff to $\hat\mu$: $\mu$ is P iff $\hat\mu$ is.
By (i)-(iii) the T-moves of $\hat p$ are the images of those of $p$ (so a T-move exists in $\hat p$ iff in $p$), and the K-moves of $\hat p$ are the images of the K-moves of $p$, with children $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$. $\qquad\blacksquare$

*Remark.* The argument never uses the phase of the wall (which colour stands on file $c$) or any property of the files outside $A$. It also shows that the only role of the cut is to guarantee that $A\subset$ pattern files (the hypothesis); it is not otherwise special (H6).

## 3. Hypotheses of Lemmas 2 and 3 for $P_n$
**H1 (wall, pattern file).** With the definition of section 2, the wall of $P_n$ is files $6..n-1$, alternating $W2$ (even $j$) and $B4$ (odd $j$): type E, black pawn two ranks above the white one. In the nodes of $R_n$ ($n\ge14$) files $7..n-1$ always equal their start content, so the exact-content reading costs nothing: they are pattern files.

**H2 (phase, ends).** $E_n$ has $W2$ on odd files and ends with $W2$ on file $n-1$; $P_n$ has $W2$ on even files, starts with $W2$ on file 6 (next to $W3B6$) and ends with $B4$ on file $n-1$ (next to $W5$ on file 0). Lemma 2(b) uses only: the capturer stands on $j+1$ (a $Y$ pawn), the $X$ pawn on $j+2$ is blocked by the $Y$ pawn on $j+3$ (the cases $W2\to3$, $W2\to4$ e.p., $B4\to3$ of the proof of Lemma 2(b) in Section S13), or the mirror image with the window $j-3..j+1$; and, when $Y$ already has a passed pawn after the move, the move is L. Lemma 3 uses only V1-V3 and Lemma 2: the views of pawns are compared by content, and the new files carry the pattern for either phase (the inserted pair $(x_{c+1},x_c)$ keeps period 2). Neither uses a file's parity or a wall end. The content assumed is only on the arc $c-4..c+5$ (resp. $j-3..j+3$) of pattern files; everything outside the arc is arbitrary. The outside of the arc is one cyclic arc and is left unchanged by $\mathrm{ins}_{12}$. For $n=18$ the arc is $8..17$, it ends at file $n-1$, and the outside is files $0..7$; for $n>18$ the outside is files $18..n-1$ together with $0..7$ and contains both $n-1$ and $0$. Either way the wrap at the zone is harmless.
*An end case.* At $n=18$ the pawn $W2$ on file $16=n-2$ has the window $13..17$ on its left (the window on its right would need file 0, which holds $W5$). Its single step is P (the reply is the capture by $B4$ on file 15), but its double step is L, not P: it lands on rank 4, so $B4$ on file 17 has no white pawn ahead of it on files $16,17,0$ ($W5$ is behind it) and becomes passed. This is the branch "if $Y$ has a passed pawn, the move is L" of Lemma 2(b). In $p$ and in $\mathrm{ins}_{12}(p)$ this pawn lies on a central file ($16=c+4$, resp. $18=c+6$) and its moves are L or P in both, so nothing breaks. (Computed: this double step is L in all 813 nodes at $n=18$; for $n=20$ it is P.)

**H3 ($q$ cannot capture).** Under Lemma 2's hypotheses files $j\pm1$ hold only the other colour's pattern pawn, two ranks further on, so the capture square is empty. An e.p. capture by $q=B4$ would need a white pawn that just stepped $2\to4$ on file $j\pm1$, but then that file is not a pattern file; $q=W2$ is on rank 2 and cannot capture e.p. (This justifies that the case analysis of Lemma 2(b) in Section S13 lists only forward steps.)

**H4 (race rule).** Lemma 2 never invokes the race (it shows $Z$ has no passed pawn). In Lemma 3, V3 gives that $c_\mu$ and $\mathrm{ins}_c(c_\mu)$ have the same passed pawns (same views; the new pawns stay blocked), with the same rank, colour, own-file occupancy and e.p. protection, hence the same class T/L/non-terminal under "count" (and under any rule that is a function of the passed pawns and of who moved). In (iii) the near replies never give $Y$ a passed pawn (Lemma 2(a)), so no race is won by $Y$. The proof itself is therefore not specific to $P_n$ or to "count"; the *value* is (S6: under the rule "mover" the signature is NRRRRRRR and $P_n\ne\star2$).

**H5 (start).** $\mathrm{start}_n$ has no passed pawn: $W5$(0) is blocked by $B7$(1); $W4$(2) by $B7$(1); $W4$(3) by $B7$(3); $W3$(5) by $B6$(4); $W2$(even $j$) by $B4$ on $j\pm1$ (file 6: $B4$(7)); $B7$(1) by $W5$(0); $B7$(3) by $W4$(2); $B6$(4) by $W4$(3); $B6$(5) by $W3$(5); $B4$(odd $j$) by $W2$ on $j-1$ (rank 2 < 4; for $j=n-1$ via $W2$(n-2), the $W5$ on file 0 is irrelevant). No flag. Hand check of the insertion: files $0..12$ are unchanged; the new files are copies of file 13 ($B4$) and file 12 ($W2$); the result alternates $W2$ (even) / $B4$ (odd) from file 6 on and has $n+2$ files, so $\mathrm{ins}_{12}(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ (also confirmed by A's pump at $c=12$).

**H6 (zone, cut).** Zone $Z_0=\{0,2,3,4,5,6\}$ (file 1 = $B7$ never changes); the wall files $7..n-1$ are outside it. Admissible cuts need $c-4\ge7$ and $c+5\le n-1$, i.e. $11\le c\le n-6$; take $c=12$, files $8..17$. The arc does not wrap iff $n\ge18=n_0$. Unlike the zones of $O_n$, $E_n$, $Z_0$ lies left of $c$, does not contain file $n-1$, and is not shifted by $\mathrm{ins}_{12}$. $n_0=18$ is forced only by the radius 5 (smallest even $n$ with ten wall files $\ge7$): $R_n$ already has 813 nodes and the same zone for $n=14,16$, which are covered by C2'.
*The cut enters only through the hypotheses.* In every node of $R_n$ the files $7..n-1$ hold the period-2 wall, so inserting one period $(x_{c+1},x_c)$ after any file $c$ with $7\le c\le n-2$ gives the same position: $\mathrm{ins}_c(p)=\mathrm{ins}_{12}(p)$ for all nodes $p$ and all such $c$ (checked for all 813 nodes at $n=18$; the pump check $R_{n+2}=\mathrm{ins}_c(R_n)$ passes for every $c=7..n-2$ and fails only for $c=6$, which cuts the zone). The radius-5 arc and hence the range $11\le c\le n-6$ is only what Lemma 3 needs to be applicable; the pump at $c=12$ is not sensitive to the choice.
No other property of $O_n$, $E_n$ is used in the proof of Section S13: Lemma 1 is about the game, Lemmas 2, 3 about the wall, and the Theorem's proof about the base graph (C1), the cut and $\mathrm{ins}_c(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$. The only places where the family enters are C1', C2' and H5/H6.

**H8 (heaps).** *Meaning.* As in Section S13 (model paragraph, Lemma 1, Theorem), "$P_n=\star2$" means: for every nim-heap $\star h$ ($h<256$ in the model of Section S13, where a passed pawn is worth $\pm256$; the step below uses no bound) $P_n+\star h$ and $\star2+\star h$ have the same outcome, namely N for $h\ne2$ and P for $h=2$. It is the whole-board/heap-sum convention; it does not assert $P_n+X\equiv\star2+X$ for an arbitrary game $X$. *Large heaps.* The programs compute the outcome of $G+\star h$ for $h=0..3$ (and $0..7$): N, N, P, N (NNPNNNNN). For every $h\ge3$ no computation is needed: $G+\star h$ has the heap move $\star h\to\star2$ to $G+\star2$, a P-position, so $G+\star h$ is N (the start has no flag, so this heap move is an ordinary move of the sum). Thus the outcomes of $P_n+\star h$ and $\star2+\star h$ agree for all $h$. *E.p. across a heap move.* Section S13 does not say whether a pending e.p. flag survives a heap move. It does not matter for the proof: the nodes of $R_n$ carry no flag, K-children never carry one, and the L/P arguments of Lemma 1 are direct replies that involve no heap move. For the unreduced searches (C2', S2) both readings ("keep", `cylcgt`'s sum semantics; "expire", textbook chess) were run by E and give identical node counts and signatures for every even $n=8..60$.

## 4. Finite checks
**C1' ($n_0=18$).** $R_{18}$ has 813 nodes, 1643 K-moves (all to distinct children) and 1372 T-moves (555 (node, side) pairs have one, so B's 2198 = 1643 + 555 distinct (node, side, target) triples); no node has an e.p. flag; no node has a passed pawn; every node agrees with $\mathrm{start}_{18}$ outside files $\{0,2,3,4,5,6\}$; solving the reduced game gives signature NNPN for $h=0..3$ (NNPNNNNN for $h\le7$), i.e. $G+\star2$ is a P-position.
Sources: A (also nodes/zone/flags for every even $n\le60$: 813 and the same zone from $n=14$); B (node and edge sets identical to A for $n=8..22$; node strings include any e.p. token, so flags and zone agree); C (813, 1643, 1372, flagged 0, touched files $\{0,2,3,4,5,6\}$, NNPN, $n=8..24$); D (the same numbers for every even $n=14..36$; 745, 1139, 889 nodes at $n=8,10,12$); E (graph identical to C's, node by node, T-sets and K-sets, for all 27 even $n=8..60$, and equal to A's output: 0 differences). Third route: the canonical form of $R_n$ in `cylcgt`'s CGT arithmetic is exactly $\star2$ for $n=8..20$.

**C2' (n = 8..16).** Unreduced search for $G+\star h$ (no poison pruning): NNPN for $n=8,10,12,14,16$ in A (27 values, $n=8..60$), in C ($n=8..22$), in D ($n=8..26,30,36$) and in E (all even $n=8..60$, both e.p. readings; for $n=8,10$ also an exhaustive solver that evaluates every child of every reachable state, 100851 and 687117 states). `cylcgt` whole-board value of $P_8$, $P_{10}$ is $\star2$.

**Insertion on the actual graphs (S1).** $\mathrm{ins}_{12}(R_n)=R_{n+2}$ (nodes onto nodes, K-edges, T-flags, T-counts) for the 21 steps $n=18..58$ in C and E (42 of 42 ok), and for $n=18..44$ in D (also $c=11$).

**Lemma 3 and 2 on the actual nodes (sanity).** C: all nodes of $R_{18}$, $R_{20}$ and all admissible cuts: 4580 and 7832 node-side-cut checks, 0 mismatches; E re-did this for $n=18,20,22,26$ (4580, 7832, 11084, 17588 checks, 0 mismatches), and with the arc requirement dropped it finds 774 and 422 mismatches at $c=5,6$ ($n=18$), so the test can fail. D: Lemma 2(a) and (b) on every move of every wall pawn with pattern neighbours (11382, 13821, 21138 moves at $n=18,20,26$; 0 captures, 0 passed-pawn violations, no T or K move); Lemma 3 on every node plus 1, 2 or 3 arbitrary moves (up to 32807 cut checks at $n=18$, 78620 at $n=20$, 76314 at $n=24$), on exhaustive local positions with 2-4 arbitrary outside files (1243, 49149, 109748 positions per phase) and on random walks: 0 mismatches; arcs of 2 and 4 files fail (897 and 99 mismatches), arcs of 6 files and longer pass, so radius 5 is conservative. C random tests with the $P$ phase: Lemma 2 (a) 9220 moves, (b) 6992 moves, 0 failures; Lemma 3 1857 accepted positions, 0 mismatches; with the arc shortened by 3 files the same test finds a mismatch (1 of 42 accepted).

## 5. Proof of the Theorem
Let $n\ge18$ be even and let $I_n$ say: no node of $R_n$ has a flag, and every node agrees with $\mathrm{start}_n$ outside $Z_0$. $I_{18}$ is C1'.
*Step.* Assume $I_n$. Every node $p$ of $R_n$ is non-terminal (no passed pawn), has no flag, and its files $8..17$ are wall files $\ge7$ outside $Z_0$, so they hold their start content: they are pattern files (H1, H6). Lemma 3 with $c=12$ applies to every node: for each side the K-children of $\mathrm{ins}_{12}(p)$ are the $\mathrm{ins}_{12}$-images of those of $p$, and the T-flags agree. As $\mathrm{ins}_{12}(\mathrm{start}_n)=\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ (H5), induction on the distance from the root shows that the nodes, K-edges and T-flags of $R_{n+2}$ are the $\mathrm{ins}_{12}$-images of those of $R_n$. Images have no flag, and since $Z_0\subset[0,6]$ lies left of the cut, $\mathrm{ins}_{12}(p)$ agrees with $\mathrm{start}_{n+2}$ outside $Z_0$: $I_{n+2}$ holds.
So $R_n\cong R_{18}$ for all even $n\ge18$ (nodes, edges, T-flags). By C1', $G+\star2$ is a P-position of the reduced game; by Lemma 1 it is a P-position of $P_n+\star2$. The signature of $G+\star h$ is NNP for $h=0,1,2$ and, for every $h\ge3$, $G+\star h$ is N by the heap move to $G+\star2$ (H8); this is the outcome of $\star2+\star h$ for every $h$, i.e. $P_n=\star2$ (H8 for the meaning). For $n=8,\dots,16$ use C2' (the same H8 step applies). $\qquad\blacksquare$ (T18: PROVED given L1-L3, L3', C1'; T: with C2'.)

## 6. Gaps and caveats
1. **No gap in the hypotheses.** Nothing in Lemmas 1-3 of Section S13 or in the Theorem's induction uses a property of $O_n$/$E_n$ beyond the wall; the differences (phase, ends, zone location, $c=12$, $n_0=18$) were checked one by one (H2, H5, H6). The only repairs are precisions: the definition of "pattern file" (section 2), the explicit bound $n\ge n_0$ (H6), the no-capture remark (H3), the large-heap step and the meaning of "$=\star2$" (H8), and the written-out step (iii) (2b).
2. **Lemmas 1-3 are cited, not re-proved, except Lemma 3 (ii)-(iii).** Their hand proofs are those of Section S13. The race rule is not defined in Section S13; H4 states it. Lemma 3 (iii) was terse in Section S13; 2b replaces it. **2b is new text, so the hand proof of T18 rests on Lemmas 1-2 of Section S13, on 2b, and on C1'.** The correspondence that 2b proves was tested by programs D and E with 0 mismatches (section 4), which is evidence but not proof.
3. **C1', C2' are computer facts, not hand proofs.** The theorem for $n\ge18$ is "proved modulo C1'". Programs A, B, C, D, E agree on C1' and A, C, D, E on C2' (B is `cylcgt`'s own code). All were written from one rule description (A, C, D, E share the model but not code; E shares only the position encoding with C); a misreading of the rules common to all of them would not be caught, apart from E's differential test against `pawns.py` (0 mismatches on about 61k positions, 690k child verdicts, 2.9k e.p. captures). The unreduced searches short-circuit on the first winning move; the version that evaluates every child was run only for $n=8,10$ (E); for $n\ge12$ the results rest on short-circuit solvers (C and E agree node for node).
4. **Scope.** Whole-board game only. In $R_{18}$, 192 of 813 nodes split into $\ge2$ components and 58 of 240 K-captures split the ring, so Lemma 1 is not available in `cylcgt`'s default component-sum model; $P_n=\star2$ there is not covered by this note. **Race rule.** The result is for the rule "count" (the project's rule, `RACE_RULE = "count"`); "opponent" gives the same signature on a different graph (881 nodes), but under "mover" (the mover wins every race) $P_n$ is not $\star2$ (NRRRRRRR, 553 nodes). The proof's lemmas are rule-independent (H4); C1' is not.
5. **Redundant evidence.** S1, S2 are CHECKED-2 up to $n=60$ (A, C, E) and are not used beyond what H7 gives. S3 (`cylcgt` values) covers $n\le20$ only and is COMPUTED-1: the whole-board `cylcgt` computation was completed for $n\le10$ only (its run for $n=12$ did not finish), so the whole-board `cylcgt` route is not a second program for C2' beyond $n=10$ (C2' stands on A, C, D, E).
6. $n=8,10,12$ have different graphs (745, 1139, 889 nodes; zones contain files 7 or 9), so they are not instances of the pump; only $n\ge14$ share $R_{18}$.
